title: Quantization prefetch planner and late-cast optimizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce per-token overhead from dequant and multiple kernel boundary copies during prefill and decode by building two coordinated runtime components: (1) a Quantization Prefetch Planner that groups incoming requests into prefetch windows with aligned precision/shape and issues combined KV allocation + shadow mapping operations; and (2) a Late-Cast Optimizer that delays dequantization/casting until the last possible kernel boundary and rewrites kernel invocation sequences to use transient view/cast operands rather than materializing full FP buffers.

Scope and motivation: Current end-to-end p95 decode latency shows a 6-12% hit on long-context models and 10-20% GPU memory churn for mixed INT8/FP8 pipelines. Profiling shows frequent small dequant ops around attention kernels and repeated materialization of casted KV caches during prefill when concurrent requests have divergent precision lanes. This ticket implements a planner + optimizer to: (a) amortize dequant work across microbatches; (b) avoid duplicated KV shadow copies; (c) prefer mixed-precision-friendly kernel invocations (e.g., fused int8-attn fastpaths) where empirically beneficial; and (d) provide safe fallback when memory or model compatibility prevents the optimizations.
acceptance_criteria: p95 decode latency improvement >= 5% on selected INT8/FP8 benchmark suite compared to baseline
GPU memory churn during sustained prefill workload reduced by >= 15% (measured by peak resident set / epoch)
End-to-end functional parity on >95% of evaluation prompts (no semantic regressions beyond tolerance), with documented failure modes
Feature gated behind runtime flags with canary rollout to 5% traffic and automatic rollback on error rate >0.5%
Observability: new telemetry for 'late_cast_saved_bytes', 'prefetch_merge_count', and per-kernel cast_time_ms logged to metrics backend
design_decisions: Planner operates at the request queue layer and exposes candidate windows of requests to the scheduler; decisions are based on token length quantiles and declared model precision compatibility

Late-Cast will prioritize in-place transient casts that map to kernel-friendly views; only materialize persistent FP caches if necessary (e.g., for incompatible kernels or when eviction thresholds are crossed)
Kernel-selection hints are advisory: runtime profiler will collect per-route statistics and may override planner hints if fused kernels show consistent regressions
Memory safety: when combined window allocation would exceed a soft memory threshold, planner will split windows and attach a backpressure signal to caller (respecting SLOs)
Compatibility: default opt-in for verified model families; new model onboarding requires a small calibration run to decide safe fastpaths
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces redundant dequant ops, lowers memory churn, can unlock fused-attn INT8 fastpaths for many workloads
Cons: added scheduling latency when forming windows (tunable), complexity in rollback and telemetry, potential for rare semantic differences if kernels are numerically divergent
Edge case: single-request long-context scenarios may not benefit and could regress slightly due to planner overhead; rollout will monitor and exclude those routes if needed
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): implement planner prototype that groups requests by model+precision and emits testable windows; collect baseline metrics
Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement late-cast primitive APIs in runtime: transient cast views, lazy materialization hooks, and kernel hint annotations
Phase 3 (2 weeks): integrate kernel selection hints and fallback policies; unit and microbench suites for INT8/FP8 combos
Phase 4 (1 week): end-to-end performance testing in staging with 3 model families; implement feature flag + canary rollout
Phase 5 (ongoing): iterate on heuristics, add telemetry dashboards, and document model onboarding flow
tasks: API: transient cast view + lazy materialize (ENG-612345-2)
Kernel: add hint plumbing to fused-attn and generic-attn paths (ENG-612345-3)
Tests: deterministic regression harness and perf microbench (ENG-612345-4)
Integration: feature flag, canary, rollback triggers (ENG-612345-5)
Docs: engineering playbook + model calibration instructions (ENG-612345-6)
observability_and_metrics: per-route p50/p95 decode latency delta compared to baseline (tagged by model, precision)
alerts: regression if p95 increases by >3% or error rate >0.5% post-canary
test_plan: Unit tests for transient cast view semantics and materialization path coverage
Microbench: 1k sample synthetic workload covering short/medium/long contexts and mixed precision lanes
Staging soak: 48-hour replay of production traces with performance and correctness assertions
A/B canary: 5% traffic routing for 72 hours with automated comparisons and manual signoff before ramp
rollback_and_mitigation: Immediate feature-flag rollback to disable planner+late-cast
Automatic fallback to conservative per-request casting if memory thresholds exceeded
Postmortem checklist: capture trace IDs, representative payloads, kernel telemetry and heap snapshots
Hotfix path: revert kernel hint plumbing if fused path causes numeric instability
